name: Walker
slug: Walker is a half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen, originally from La-rel and now Gatekeeper of The Reach.
description: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter, bonded to the mind-linked dragon Glimmen. Walker is originally from La-rel and is the only party member known to have come from outside Midgard. He is now the Gatekeeper of The Reach, responsible for protecting and exploring the largest Arch, a role well suited to him and Glimmen because of their ability to fly.

log.summary:
Edit

Walker joins Gerk in taking on his new responsibility out of loyalty and friendship, despite initially not understanding the significance of the Great Tree. He considers Glimmen part of the group and jokingly argues that she deserves a crown. As the only party member originally from outside Midgard, Walker is offered the La-rel keystone but declines it, choosing The Reach instead because La-rel represents his past while The Reach better reflects who he has become. He receives The Reach keystone and becomes its Gatekeeper, taking responsibility for protecting and exploring the largest Arch. Walker and Glimmen are particularly well suited to traveling the Reach due to their ability to fly. He is also able to see the mysterious white-flower girl and her trail, and recognizes a distinctive tree after Gerk opens a portal to a forest, helping identify the location as being near Langdale. Walker is eager to use the portal to travel back toward home. The Raven Queen notes that Walker and Ord have impressed her less than some of the others, though they have still demonstrated qualities beyond what she normally sees in mortals.

log.summary: Walker plans to return to The Reach with Glimmen, Plymouth Gawater, Elrus, and Araden to scout the Dragon Rider training grounds for clues related to his vision of Grixto and Galixtar near the caves. He intends to keep Elrus and Araden as secret weapons, carry the party's sending stone for updates, recharge his gems, and retreat if necessary rather than seek a fight. Walker uses his keystone to activate the gate to The Reach, despite its portal's size being insufficient to bring the party's boat through. He notes that his former roost appears empty and that he previously explored the area without encountering Grixto. He also recognizes that The Reach's time difference may allow him to spend much longer there than the party experiences in Midgard. Walker describes The Reach as an autumnal setting with crisp weather, early fall colors, and the National Flying League beginning its season, alongside floating jack-o'-lanterns and other flying elements.

log.summary: Walker travels with Plymouth Gawater and Elrus on a side excursion into The Reach via portal cube near the Whispering Abyss, planning a multi-day flight north to the Dragon Rider training grounds during a broader forty-nine-day Reach stay that costs dragon energy and inflicts daily exhaustion unless he changes course. He has quit alcohol and uses nicotine as a temporary substitute, learns basic SOS fire signals without gaining proficiency, and opens mind-link contact with Ciri while separated. A detour over Sunder leads him to Qualin's Quax, where failed perception leaves him fixated on Quaylin's heirloom gem and unable to afford potions of vitality. He seeks Hanzuni at Haven Hold for a quest-based gold loan rather than trigger a Sunder Chase, citing Quaylin's referral. Walker reveals his golden hand is plated flesh—not metal—a removable thirty-pound replica he believes turned gold after touching cold molten-looking water, possibly near the Temple of I; Quaylin confirms it with a pestle. He carries about eight hundred twenty-six gold and sixty-one platinum locally with roughly ten thousand gold left in Langdale, wears mismatched star gem earrings from a past hoard fight, and declines trading them for matching pairs from Hanzuni.
notes: Is traveling with Plymouth Gawater on a short side excursion, using a portal cube to exit into The Reach near the Whispering Abyss.

log.summary: Walker leaves Hanzuni's hoard room at Haven Hold on his own training schedule, with no meeting set with Elrus or Araden. The regimen has left him with one level of exhaustion and disadvantage on ability checks. Under a sevenfold time difference, about a week of party travel is roughly a month for him; the others fly home to meet him, and from the stronghold he is expected back in about two days, with Sylan taking an earlier check-in as a sign he is fine. He does not go to Carlkin. He meets Elrus and Araden and, after Plymouth finishes an errand, travels with them from Sunder to the training island, not remembering why until the Grixto hideaway lead is restored. Sylan has told him to retreat rather than fight if Grixto is there. He rolls a 21 on Perception, finds the hidden ledge and crevice, leaves Araden outside with Elrus as a mental relay and Plymouth searching the guild stronghold, and signals Elrus by tapping his head. Bow drawn, he climbs the narrow path toward the smell of death (passive Perception 18), hears faint humming and two stones tapping, and has Elrus bring Plymouth down. Approaching the roost with Glimmen, he fails a disadvantaged Stealth check with a 10. He recognizes the cavern from Emhet's vision, notes the smaller side has changed slightly, refuses Vecna's request to help retrieve a book, and walks in. His replacement arm and hand are compared to Vecna's; both losses are tied to a battle over an item the party reached first.
notes: He leaves Hanzuni's hoard room at Haven Hold on his own training schedule, with no meeting time set with Elrus or Araden. The regimen has given him one level of exhaustion and disadvantage on ability checks.

About a week of travel for the party is roughly a month for him under a sevenfold time difference. The others are flying home to meet him. From the party's side at the stronghold, he is expected back in about two days, and Sylan treats an earlier check-in as evidence he is fine.

He does not go to Carlkin. He meets Elrus and Araden and, after Plymouth finishes an errand, travels with them from Sunder to the training island. He does not remember why they are going until the DM restores the Grixto hideaway lead. Sylan has told him to retreat rather than fight if Grixto is there.

He rolls a 21 on Perception, finds the hidden ledge and crevice, and investigates. He leaves Araden outside, Elrus as a mental relay, and Plymouth searching the guild stronghold with orders not to wander too far. He signals Elrus by tapping his head.

He climbs the narrow cliff path into the crevice with his bow drawn, stalking the smell of death. His passive Perception is 18. He hears faint humming and two different stones tapping. He confirms with Elrus that the place should have been unused for centuries, then has Elrus bring Plymouth down while he continues.

He approaches the roost with Glimmen and fails a disadvantaged Stealth check with a 10; his footsteps echo. He recognizes the cavern as the room from Emhet's vision. The smaller side has changed slightly since that vision. He refuses Vecna's request to help retrieve a book and walks in.
His own arm and hand are a replacement, compared directly to Vecna's alchemical or mechanical replacement. Both losses are tied to a battle over an item the party reached first.

log.summary: Walker is away from the lighthouse on a mission with his dragon, according to Sylan. He confirms they killed Grixto once and still wears Grixto's helmet by choice; Dana says it is the only relic kept from the body and a leading phylactery suspect. In the roost cave he meets Vecna, who is seeking his book. Walker had sent Elrus in behind him. He tells Vecna he is no closer to Galixtar or the book, and that Walker is hunting Grixto, who is with Galixtar. He floats then retracts a book-for-phylactery trade. Unsure of the phylactery and sure the book is not it, he will destroy the Raskina if needed and will not owe Vecna. Recalling Emhet's vision of a young lich and the book, he guesses Valkyrie's skin, rejects killing a sister for power, and stops Vecna when restoration is offered. He knows Valkyries only as warrior-angels and says his family is dead. He takes a miniature Raskina and red quill without a deal. Investigation 11 yields tilted carvings. He thinks Galixtar died before Grixto's lichdom, so Grixto wants the Al Kurin to restore her, and Elrus takes him to the ruined tower; that search is unresolved.
notes: Not at the lighthouse. Sylan says the dragon is away on a mission. Walker briefly confirms that they did kill Grixto once. He took Grixto's helmet and still wears it as a style choice. Dana says it is the only thing he kept from the body, and it is a leading phylactery suspect.

Finds Vecna waiting in the roost cave, looking for his book. Walker had sent Elrus in behind him. He tells Vecna that Vecna is no nearer to Galixtar or the book, and that he himself is after Grixto, who is with Galixtar.

Proposes that if he comes to hold the book and Vecna comes to hold the phylactery, they could trade, then walks that back from an agreed exchange. He does not know what the phylactery is, is sure Vecna's book is not it, and says he will destroy the Raskina if it turns out to be the phylactery. Out of character he does not want to be indebted to Vecna.

Does not remember Emhet's vision at first, then recalls a young lich with the book visible. He guesses the book was made from Valkyrie's skin, refuses any interest in killing a sister for power, and stops Vecna when told the book can restore lost people, things, or beings. He knows Valkyries only in a general warrior-angel sense. He says all his family is dead.

Agrees it is fair to worry that the darkness in the book may not be worth recovering. He thinks Vecna responds better to a little insolence than to open fear. He is polite and a little sharp in the room, wishes Vecna luck, and admits he was scared once he is out of sight.

Accepts a miniature Raskina and a red quill despite dreading the bargain, because writing in it is how he can contact Vecna later. He does not close a deal. His Investigation of 11 maps the cave and turns up tilted carvings rather than a phylactery.

Theorizes that Galixtar died before Grixto became a lich, and that restoring her is why Grixto wants the Al Kurin. He has Elrus take him to the ruined tower because he has an idea about the tilted carvings. From that vantage he starts another investigation, which is not resolved.

log.summary: Walker stays alone on the Reach while Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are with Carlkin. He spoke with Vecna, which the DM treats as communication begun and possibly a book club, but he does not want to speak again immediately and will not write in the book to ask if Vecna is still below. His time runs about seven days to each party day: since they left he has lived about eleven days (a little over two for them), and by the practice morning about forty-two of his days have passed after five days and a morning of party time. He promised to check in after one Midgar week, so they are not yet due to hear from him. The party's clock controls the split; when the week ends his remaining time is montaged and he rejoins unless he stops early. In the Dragon Rider guild keep ruins he matches cave drawings to the surface. His sketch of an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain is rotated from the old guild tower, and he thinks the record is incomplete; the thread last ended on an earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil, and he found no map, compass, or written plan. A deity-left-the-realm notice brings him and Glimmen back to an empty room. He had not been taught the Weave or ley lines, reads the etchings' shared offset as a clue, and wants the ley-line landmark. He sets the troop markers, pockets the hunched eagle Vecna had been tapping, later hands it over, and guesses it is a tuning fork. He agrees the convergence is the best lead and meditates in the cave with Elrus on Grixto's puzzle until Elrus uses the table; the cutaway leaves him there. He spends energy and takes exhaustion to charge gems that now glow, hoping to learn primal stones. Near a conveyance his wards and shields would be amplified, then fade after he leaves, and untrained channeling could channel him out of existence. He is expected back at the stronghold on Glimmen rather than by carriage, invited to contact the others once told they went south into the forest, with the stronghold ready to feed the dragon.
notes: Spoke with Vecna, which the DM treats as Walker having started communicating with him, and he may now be in a book club with Vecna. He does not want to speak to Vecna again immediately.

On the Reach alone while Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are with Carlkin. About five days and a morning of party time have passed since they left him; he has lived about eleven days, counted as a little over two days for them. His time runs about seven days to each party day. By the practice morning about forty-two of his days have passed. He promised to check in after one Midgar week of their time, so they are not yet due to hear from him.
The party's clock controls the split. When their one-week window ends, his remaining time is montaged and he rejoins, unless he stops early.

He is in the Dragon Rider guild keep ruins, matching cave drawings to the surface. His sketch of an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain is rotated from the view at the old guild tower, and he thinks the record is incomplete. His separate thread last ended on an earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil. He found no map, compass, or written plan.
He left the cave because Vecna was there and will not write in the book to ask if Vecna is still below. A deity-left-the-realm notice brings him and Glimmen back to an empty room.
He had not been taught the Weave or ley lines. He reads the shared offset of the etchings as a clue and wants to reach the ley-line landmark.

He set the troop markers on the table, pocketed the hunched eagle Vecna had been tapping, and later hands it over. He asks what an eagle has to do with a mountain or a waterfall, is told nothing, and guesses it is a tuning fork as the scene cuts away.

He agrees the convergence is the best lead and meditates in the cave with Elrus on Grixto's puzzle. He still does not understand what he was told to look for until Elrus uses the table. The cutaway leaves him in that meditation.

He has been spending energy and taking exhaustion to charge gems that now glow, and he hopes to learn primal stones. Near a conveyance his wards and shields would be amplified, then fade after he leaves. Untrained channeling could channel him out of existence.
Expected back at the stronghold on Glimmen rather than by carriage, and invited to contact the others once told they went south into the forest. The stronghold is to be ready to feed the dragon.

log.summary: Walker spoke with Vecna until Vecna left and learned what a ley-line convergence is. On Elrus's advice he flew to the obelisk with Plymouth Gawater, without having told Elrus of the convergence, and still wants Elrus's table in Nyx checked. Fire is the element he learned first; he can also call water, light, and darkness and spend energy stored in gemstones. He does not remember a cosmic loom. He considered primal stones in his helmet for night vision, heat, and sight through magical darkness, but drops that unless the helmet can see what he wants. He carries a heat stone from Nyx Cage and a keystone, leaves the keystone unmodified, and will not feed the heat stone more magic after an implosion warning. He reconstructs the ley-line offset as about half a degree (0.01 radians); his corrected return is from the tower, 0.01 radians west, then 5.6 miles. Elrus's watch shows 42 days of training to Walker's roughly two weeks, and he will not imbue a primal stone yet. He and Plymouth lightning-teleport above the stronghold on the morning of the eighth day and return with Glimmen and Araden. Bound for New Navel and then Grazog, he instead flies after Dana when the black beacon rises. Rejoined, he gives the recognition lines and will not say whether the hat, the party's phylactery candidate, has corrupted him.
notes: Last session he spoke with Vecna in the cave, waited until Vecna left, and learned what a ley-line convergence is.
He flies to the convergence obelisk on Elrus's advice, with Plymouth Gawater aboard, and also wants Elrus's table in Nyx checked for another gold eagle or more information.

Fire is the element he learned first and treats as primary. He can also call water, light, and darkness, and he can spend energy already stored in gemstones. Dragon-linked people can move that stored energy safely. He had not told Elrus he had found a convergence.

He does not remember a cosmic loom. He is considering primal stones and wants them set in his helmet for night vision, heat detection, and sight through magical darkness. He already has darkvision, can breathe underwater, and carries a heat stone. He will not use the personal jewelry he worked hard to make, and he drops the project unless the helmet can see what he wants.

He carries a heat stone bought in Agenheim from Nyx Cage and a keystone. He jokes about modifying the keystone, then accepts Plymouth's refusal. After the implosion warning he will not feed the heat stone more magic.

At the obelisk he reconstructs a lost note: mountain to the west, obelisk to the north, about twenty degrees off the ley line. Facing the guild, the true line is about a hundred yards to the right. He restates that offset as about half a degree, or 0.01 radians.
He agrees to leave, gather more stones and energy, and return. His return pin, after he corrects an earlier 'two miles northwest,' is from the tower, 0.01 radians west, then 5.6 miles.

Elrus's watch says Walker has been training for exactly 42 days. Walker experienced about two weeks. He will not imbue a primal stone yet; he wants the party's advice. His own idea is night vision. He also suggests a bard instrument for Dana and says the cosmic loom still has to be sorted out before he knows whether a stone helps.

He has not contacted the stronghold group during this absence. He and Plymouth arrive by lightning teleport on the mountain above the stronghold, marked there by thunder on the morning of the eighth day. He returns from the training full of energy, with Glimmen and Araden.

He means to drop Plymouth Gawater at New Navel and then go to Grazog. One or two gatehouse guards hail him. When the black beacon rises he tells Elrus the plan has changed, leaves the Grazog trip, and flies after Dana. Glimmen overtakes her broom.
On arrival he asks what is going on. A claim of being gone forty-nine days is a joke he immediately walks back. He sees the beacon vanish when the staff is released.

He is back with the party as the two dragons land beside the forest. He supplies the recognition lines 'I don't trust the cat man,' 'scoop fruit,' and 'loincloth,' and jokes that Sylan should claim to be Gerk's dad.

The hat he has been wearing is the party's candidate for the lich's phylactery. Sylan remembers the first time Walker put it on as questionable. Asked if it has corrupted him, Walker does not answer directly.

log.summary: Walker says Vecna, at the old training grounds, is alive and their friend, treating the result as common interests, not a completed deal. Vecna wants the sister-skin book back and had passed it off as rat skin; Walker reads Vecna tapping the golden eagle as a hint. The eagle lights the war-table map. He thinks it is half a pair, the other half at Vecna's former palace in Nyx. He has worn the white helm the whole time and will hand it only to Carlkin. He doubts it is the phylactery and would destroy one only with eyes on its owner. If Grixto influences either of them, it would be Glimmen; Walker's fire can protect Glimmen through their bond. He is fire resistant, not fireproof, and carries a golden glove. Elrus pauses meditation with Benji during the helm study. He stays at the lighthouse with Dana, Ord, and Ciri, recovering it from the smoldering pouch. After killing the emperor he spoke with a different hobgoblin in purple robes, who called the golden fire his life force. Carlkin finds slight, non-parasitic soul contact. Walker puts the helm on to track the emperor. Araden, Glimmen, and the party's whispers are familiar voices.
notes: He flies back from the old training grounds, where he spoke briefly with Vecna. Asked whether he is alive and still their friend, he says, "Why wouldn't I be here?" He frames the result as common interests rather than a completed deal, after first allowing they might have made one.
Vecna wants the sister-skin book back and had tried to pass it off as rat skin. Vecna was tapping the golden eagle. Walker now reads that as a hint. At the time he thought Vecna was bored.

Placing the eagle on the war-table map lights the map. Walker thinks it is one half of a pair and that the other half is at Vecna's former palace in Nyx. He has not had the eagle the whole time. He expects Sylan to know the capital's name. Sylan does not.

He has been wearing the white helm the whole time, including during two remote contacts, and says he grabbed it, which is why it is the only piece of that armor still remaining. He calls it his helmet, doubts it is mundane or the phylactery, and says it is extraordinary and worn over the nose.
He will not give the helm to the party. He will let Carlkin examine it and will hand it only to Carlkin. He agrees a phylactery should be destroyed only when they have eyes on its owner.

He says that if Grixto is influencing either of them, it would be Glimmen. His internal fire can spread and protect Glimmen through their bond. He is fire resistant, does not believe he is fireproof, and carries a golden glove. Ciri starts a tinderbox under his arm as a test.

Elrus is training him in meditation and introduces him to Benji as the new recruit. That training pauses while the helm is investigated, then resumes. He goes to Carlkin's with Dana, Ord, and Ciri rather than flying off alone.

He asks why they cannot walk in on Carlkin unannounced. He agrees to stay in the lighthouse while the helm is studied. A 27 perception check lets him see Carlkin's pouch start to smolder. With his fire resistance and golden glove, the bag's heat comes to basically nothing, and he recovers the helm.

He sets the helm on the lectern in Carlkin's study. He confirms that after he killed the emperor he had a conversation with him, and that the emperor was different. He thinks he explained this to the party once. Sylan is not sure he did.

After the emperor's death, picking up the helm brought a calm, respectful conversation. The emperor was a hobgoblin in purple robes. He called the golden fire of Walker's gold dragon rider bond Walker's life force.

Carlkin finds only slight, non-parasitic contact with the soul on the helm. Walker puts the helm back on anyway and argues it is safest there. He hopes the fragment can be used to track the emperor and looks for a companion who works with souls. Sylan is not at the lighthouse.
He already counts Araden, Glimmen, and the party's whispers as familiar voices, so those would not count as the warning sign Carlkin gives him.

log.summary: Walker questioned Mahali about whether he became a god or was born one, how belief and the Weave create gods, and how gods can be killed, insisting it was mere curiosity; he admitted he was never taught about the Weave. He showed interest in freshly baked buns and the value of the gems in Ponchi's buns, and helped chop carrots and potatoes in the kitchen. Asked whom he trusts, he hesitated before naming Gerk above all else, then said he believes in all his friends. He was the only party member to loot the lich's body, and he claims the possessing helm, having resisted its possession and refusing to give it up. He previously had one pleasant conversation with Garrick through the helm and believes the party's first enemy was truly Garrick rather than a possessed proxy. He holds the Soul identifier bag and the hunched eagle marker. Declining significant protection, he wore the helm again during Sylan's extraction, passed the Wisdom save, and shared a vision of a young Grixto, who nodded respectfully to him.
